items.title: Mutation-capable projection trust envelope
items.statement: Every mutation-capable projection carries projection_state, last_observed_at, source_event_ref, and revalidation_route; projection behavior is governed by canonical runtime and storage projections instead of elapsed-time guesses.

evidence.exact_quote: - Mutation-capable projections carry projection_state, last_observed_at, source_event_ref, and revalidation_route.

Projection state, freshness, direct revalidation, degraded fallback, stale-observation waits, and timeout display are governed by canonical runtime and storage projections rather than elapsed-time guesses.

items.title: Projection mutation fail-closed behavior
items.statement: Stale, degraded, and unavailable projections disable mutation unless the owner surface directly revalidates the projection.

evidence.exact_quote: - Stale, degraded, and unavailable projections disable mutation unless the owner surface performs direct revalidation.

items.title: Canonical timeout display and recovery route
items.statement: Wait and timeout cards display the retained timeout_class and recover through stored blocked episodes or receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - Wait and timeout cards show canonical retained timeout_class and route recovery through stored blocked episodes or receipts.

items.title: Stale observation is not failure evidence
items.statement: A stale observation alone must not be interpreted as skipped or failed, and wait-copy presentation cannot mint blocked reasons, failure classes, or receipt identities.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Do not infer skipped/failed from stale observation alone."
- "Do not create new blocked reason, failure class, or receipt identity from wait-copy presentation."

items.title: Direct revalidation authority and freshness thresholds are underspecified
items.statement: The unit makes direct revalidation the exception that can re-enable mutation but does not define the authorized actor, success response, freshness threshold, concurrency rule, or state transition produced by revalidation.
items.impact: Builders could re-enable mutation under inconsistent freshness and authorization rules.
items.builder_discretion: Define the revalidation protocol only after canonical authority, threshold, and transition rules are supplied.

evidence.exact_quote: - Stale, degraded, and unavailable projections disable mutation unless the owner surface performs direct revalidation.

dimension_assessments.summary: Concrete projection, routing, notification, record, promotion, widget, and artifact behaviors are extracted.
The window specifies run-aware routing, escalation surfaces, durable project/account records, promotion reviews, Progress widgets, and domain blocked payloads.
Important fields are named, but complete route, record, review, widget, and blocked-payload schemas and invalid-input outputs are absent.
The window provides several explicit field, vocabulary, separation, and routing contracts, while identified schema gaps remain separately recorded.
State labels and separation rules exist, but revalidation, escalation, current-to-history, promotion, and terminal-precedence transitions are underspecified.
Owner identities are surfaced, but mutation revalidation, escalation, promotion decisions, reopen, and terminal conflict authority are not defined.
All units name Orchestrator_Page as owner_doc and owner hint, yet runtime owner-surface authority and mutable target ownership remain incomplete.
History, Progress, Dashboard, thread/chat/input surfaces, cross-surface attention consumers, and domain owner surfaces are identified.
GUI-related boundaries, surface allocations, Progress-only widget composition, and blocked-card presentation are explicit.
Mutation fail-closed rules, timeout recovery, canonical blocked-state preservation, missing-link handling, and stale readiness dispatch protection are explicit.
No access-control, redaction, sensitive-link, reviewer-identity, or retention policy accompanies routed identity and review evidence.
The units depend on shared state and routing contracts but declare no dependency or unblocking edges.
Operational handling includes wait/timeout recovery, active notification placement, durable histories, cost-bearing receipt routing, and blocked owner pivots.
No load envelope or latency, pagination, update, retention-size, or rendering budgets are supplied.
The Progress widget surface explicitly rejects tiers-first compatibility governance, and all units retain migration lineage and validation surfaces.
Structural migration and index validators are declared, but executable runtime and GUI behavior oracles are absent.
Consequential choices remain for revalidation, route schemas, escalation, storage lifecycle, governance transitions, catalog completeness, precedence, security, and performance.
The extracted gaps identify the unresolved contract, authority, transition, schema, dependency, oracle, privacy, and scale questions in the core.
